overview: Gyllyngvase is Falmouth’s main town beach: a sandy, south-facing bay just below the seafront hotels, a short walk from the town centre and west of Pendennis Castle. With lifeguards in season, a café, toilets and parking next to the sand, it’s an easy family beach.
Queen Mary Gardens, opened in 1910, sit right beside the beach, and the seafront walk links it with Falmouth’s other beaches.

expect.title: Town beach
expect.text: A sheltered sandy beach with everything close by.

expect.title: Queen Mary Gardens
expect.text: Formal gardens beside the beach, nice for a wander or a picnic.

expect.title: Seafront walk
expect.text: Stroll along to Swanpool in one direction or round towards Pendennis Point in the other.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: South of Falmouth town centre, below Cliff Road.

week.text: Easy to fit into any Falmouth day, and sheltered from westerly winds as it faces south-east. Pair it with Pendennis Castle or the Maritime Museum if the weather turns.

pairWith.why: another sandy beach a short walk west
Henry VIII’s castle on the headland
the maritime museum for a wet spell

tips: Walk the seafront path to Swanpool and back.
